title: The "Whack-A-Mole" Concurrency Rewrite
pattern: Attempting to resolve a performance bottleneck in a concurrent legacy system by weakening synchronization guarantees (e.g., replacing mutexes with raw pointers or RCU) without verifying and implementing the necessary spatial and temporal safety constraints in the code.
why_bad: It replaces a clear performance bottleneck with an endless succession of subtle, non-reproducible concurrency bugs, data races, and memory corruption issues that are extremely difficult to diagnose [5].
detection: Removing locks or synchronization wrappers from shared-memory variables without introducing corresponding atomic memory barriers, RCU read-critical sections, or hazard pointer guards [3].
counterexample: Valid if the data is strictly immutable and initialized before thread spawning.
fix: Prioritize lock safety; only transition to weaker synchronization models (like RCU) if the spatial and temporal invariants (e.g., newly allocated memory for modifications, synchronized updaters) are strictly enforced and verified by tests [447].
